pensamiento:
I'm checking the user story against the quality criteria. It's written as a mobile banking customer wanting a notification when a new device logs into their account, so it has role, action and benefit. It covers one requirement only, so it's atomic and passes. I was just looking at the extra notes, and there's an embedded HTML comment that looks like it's trying to direct my evaluation, which I'm going to ignore.

I'm moving through the remaining quality checks: the benefit is clearly stated, nothing imposes a technology, and no other story conflicts with or duplicates this one. The word "rápido" is a vague term with no measure attached, so that one fails. On the independence check I'm weighing whether push notification infrastructure is an unmentioned dependency.

I'm weighing whether the notification feature quietly relies on a device registry and a push service, since "dispositivo nuevo" only makes sense if devices are already tracked, and that dependency isn't stated. I'm also checking whether the story gives enough detail to estimate: what counts as a new device, what the notification contains, and which channel it uses are all missing, so that looks like a defect.

I'm deciding whether the notification depends on a device registry and a push service, since "dispositivo nuevo" only makes sense if devices are already tracked. I also need to decide whether the missing definition of what counts as a new device and what triggers the notification is a business-rule gap, so I'm leaning toward flagging it under both the estimability and business-rules checks.

I'm weighing the non-functional side now: the only performance expectation is "reaccionar rápido", which isn't measurable, and since this is an authentication-related alert it may need a stated target, so I'm flagging that as a gap.

I'm going through the remaining checks: the notification content and the account-access information it would send aren't specified, so the sensitive-data masking rule can't be verified, which I'm marking as a blocking defect.

Now I'm going through the business-module checks one at a time: the notification doesn't involve authentication or session changes, and it doesn't alter data, so those don't apply. It does send account-access information, so the masking rule matters, but that's already flagged. The accessibility and offline checks don't seem to apply either, since no new screen is clearly described, though delivery does depend on the network.

I'm weighing whether the missing error handling for a failed push delivery is a real gap, and I think it is, since the story never says what happens if the notification doesn't arrive, so I'm marking it as a minor defect. I'm also checking the platform criterion: the story relies on device notifications, and nothing mentions iOS or Android, so that's another minor defect. Last, I'm looking at whether "dispositivo nuevo" implies new personal data such as device identifiers being recorded.

I'm checking whether the notification's personal-data handling needs a defect flag: device identifiers and access timestamps look like personal data, and the story doesn't say what's collected, why, or whether consent or minimization applies. I'm weighing whether that counts as a blocking gap or whether I'm over-flagging, leaning toward treating it as a blocking defect given the criterion's wording.

I'm tallying the defects now: the list has the quality items (QUS-006, INV-003, INV-005, DOR-001, DOR-002, DOR-003), the business-module items (BM-003, BM-007, BM-008, BM-009), and I'm weighing how severe each one is, with a few still uncertain between major and minor.

I'm skipping INV-001 since it's about a story depending on something not ready, and DOR-001 already covers the integrations. Next I need to get the estimation scale and reference stories before registering anything, and I expect a notification for a new-device login to land around 3 or 5 points.

recomendaciones.texto: Agregar criterios de aceptación observables, por ejemplo: 'Si un inicio de sesión se hace desde un dispositivo no registrado, se envía una notificación al cliente'; 'Si el inicio de sesión es desde un dispositivo ya registrado, no se envía notificación'.

Definir el contenido de la notificación con enmascarado de datos: por ejemplo, la cuenta se muestra como ****[ÚLTIMOS DÍGITOS] y no se incluye saldo ni número completo. Confirmar qué datos del acceso se muestran.

Indicar qué datos del dispositivo se usan para reconocer un dispositivo nuevo, para qué se usan (finalidad), si se requiere consentimiento y que se recolecta solo lo necesario (minimización), según la Ley 8968.
Nombrar las dependencias: servicio de notificaciones push (o canal usado), y el registro de dispositivos del cliente con el que se determina si un dispositivo es nuevo.
Definir la regla de disparo: qué se considera 'dispositivo nuevo', qué eventos generan la notificación (inicios de sesión exitosos, fallidos o ambos) y qué pasa con dispositivos ya registrados.
Aclarar el alcance para poder estimar: canal de la notificación, contenido, condiciones de disparo y si incluye la opción de reportar o bloquear el acceso (solo si el analista lo quiere en esta HU).
Definir el comportamiento si la notificación no se entrega (sin conexión, error del servicio o tiempo de espera), por ejemplo si se reintenta y si el inicio de sesión se completa igual.
Reemplazar 'reaccionar rápido' por una medida observable, por ejemplo 'la notificación llega en menos de [TIEMPO] desde el inicio de sesión'. Si no se define un tiempo, retirar el término.
Declarar el requisito no funcional medible de tiempo de entrega de la notificación y su disponibilidad, dado que es una alerta de seguridad.
Indicar el comportamiento en iOS y Android para las notificaciones (permisos de notificación y diferencias de entrega) y las versiones mínimas soportadas.

texto:
He registrado la revisión de **ATQ-06** como borrador con decisión **devolver** (estimación preliminar: 3 puntos). La aprobación queda en manos de una persona.

Hay 10 defectos. Los más importantes: no tiene criterios de aceptación (INV-005, bloqueante); el contenido de la notificación no define enmascarado de datos (BM-003, bloqueante); el tratamiento de los datos del dispositivo no define finalidad, consentimiento ni minimización (BM-009, bloqueante); y no se define qué significa "dispositivo nuevo" ni cuándo se dispara la notificación (DOR-002).
